deals.evidence: Norwich City is delighted to announce that a group led by Mark Attanasio has successfully acquired a minority shareholding in the football club.
deals.headline: Attanasio-led group buys minority stake in Norwich City
deals.investor: Group led by Mark Attanasio (Norfolk FB Holdings)
deals.seller: Various holders including director Michael Foulger
deals.summary: A group led by Mark Attanasio acquired a minority shareholding from several holders, including long-serving director Michael Foulger, and Attanasio joined the board. Price and stake not stated.

deals.evidence: The group successfully passed a number of checks by the EFL to secure 40.4 percent of the club’s ordinary shares.
deals.headline: Norfolk FB Holdings becomes joint majority shareholder with 40.4%
deals.summary: After shareholders approved the increase at an October 2023 general meeting and EFL checks, Norfolk FB Holdings held 40.4% of the ordinary shares, level with Delia Smith and Michael Wynn Jones.

deals.evidence: in consideration for Norfolk Holdings capitalising certain loans which have been made available to the club, totalling approximately £59m
deals.headline: Norfolk Holdings takes majority control by capitalising about £59m of loans
deals.summary: Norfolk Holdings capitalised loans of approximately £59m into new non-voting preference shares, with no payment to Delia Smith and Michael Wynn Jones; on 2 March 2025 it converted some into ordinary shares, taking it to about 85% (85.2% at 30 June 2025) with Smith and Wynn Jones on 10%. The annual report puts the converted loans at £56.6m.

deals.evidence: Norfolk have provided further funding (through debt financing) of £29.8m.
deals.headline: Owners lend Norwich a further £29.8m
deals.summary: During 2024/25 and up to the date of the annual report (November 2025), Norfolk provided further funding of £29.8m as debt; £43.5m was owed to Norfolk at 30 June 2025.

founded_evidence: We were formed in 1902 following a meeting called by Robert Webster and Joseph Cowper Nutchey
name: Norwich City Football Club
notes: PSC register (00154044): Mark Attanasio 50-75% and Richard Ressler 25-50% (notified 31 Jan 2025), both indirect through Norfolk FB Holdings; Delia Smith and Michael Wynn Jones ceased as PSCs on 3 March 2025. The club's board page calls Attanasio 'Majority Shareholder'; a club tribute dated 29 September 2026 marks the death of Michael Wynn Jones, honorary life president, so the 10% family holding may since have passed to his estate. No chair is named on the board page, and the top executive is Executive Director Zoe Webber (no CEO title). Carrow Road ownership is not stated: the group holds freehold land and buildings of £34.5m but no page names the stadium as freehold; a charge of 25 Aug 2026 to M.P. Kemp Limited covers freehold land north of the Avant training centre. Revenue split as the club gives it (2024/25, £000): gate receipts and ticket sales 10,569; broadcasting 11,858; media 188; catering 4,191; commercial 4,975; sponsorship and advertising 4,295; UEFA solidarity 1,361; other lines small; commercial left null because it cannot be summed. Wages figure is the 'wages and salaries' line only; total wage costs were 122% of turnover. Norfolk FB Holdings is an investor group of individuals, so it is not flagged institutional. No valuation, net debt figure or social counts found; no top-flight title (five second-tier titles, latest 2020/21).

ownership_summary: Controlled by Norfolk FB Holdings LLC, the US investor group led by Mark Attanasio (Milwaukee Brewers; Crescent Capital co-founder) with Richard Ressler (CIM Group, Orchard Capital), which owned 85.2% of the issued capital at 30 June 2025 after converting loans into shares on 2 March 2025. Delia Smith and Michael Wynn Jones, majority owners from 1996, kept about 10%; other shareholders hold the rest of a widely held, unlisted PLC.
